title: Orchestrated hosted endpoint PRD: scope rebaselining, acceptance catalog, and launch plan
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: This PRD captures the rebased scope for the converged hosted inference surface (chat, completions, embeddings, rerank), defines the acceptance catalog for launch, and documents the operational rollout plan including canary slices, telemetry gates, and fallback policies. The goal is to ship a cohesive API bundle that provides predictable latency/quality tradeoffs for early enterprise customers and enables clear upgrade paths to Dedicated and Private offerings.
goals: Unify API behavior across chat/completions/embeddings/rerank with explicit acceptance tests for behavioral compatibility
Deliver launch-ready telemetry and SLOs so customers see token-level cost and latency breakdowns in Console
Establish canary and rollout recipes (1% -> 10% -> 25%) with automated rollback triggers linked to telemetry
Provide graded fallback logic to compatible model variants to ensure continuity under capacity pressure
non_goals: Full multi-tenant throughput optimization for Dedicated within this launch window
Adding new multimodal inputs (images/audio) — out of scope for this bundle
Large-scale model onboarding beyond curated set (limited to verified models only)
scope_items: Behavioral acceptance harness that runs eval suites (prompt sets) each CI run
Runtime QoS knobs surfaced in Console: batching window, kv_cache_enabled, quantization_profile
Telemetry: per-route p50/p90/p95 latency, token counts, cost estimates, error breakdowns
Rollout: staged canary slices, automated rollback via runbook, dashboard for cutover status
Fallback policies: model-variant map and regional fallthrough rules
api_contract_summary: /v1/chat: streaming and unary, support for function/tool calling, conversation metadata, max_tokens and stop semantics remain stable
/v1/completions: prompt + params parity with existing hosted surface; deterministic seeding for evals
/v1/embeddings: batch up to 512 texts, deterministic embedding vector dim by model, response tagging for model/quantization
/v1/rerank: accept query + candidates, return score array + normalized ranking metadata
acceptance_criteria: Behavioral: Acceptance harness shows <=1% regression on gold prompt sets across generation quality metrics vs baseline models
Performance: p95 request latency under target for typical request shapes (see performance_targets) and <0.5% spike incidents during 10k qps synthetic load
Reliability: error rate <0.2% at 95th percentile traffic and successful fallback engaged when primary model capacity exhausted
Telemetry: Console shows per-route token cost and latency within 30s of ingestion for production slices
Security: KMS integration validated for Private customers in smoke runs and audit logging enabled for sensitive events
Docs/SDKs: Quickstarts for Node/Python updated and example repo linked in PRD
performance_targets: Chat (single-turn, <512 tokens): p95 end-to-end latency < 180ms under typical host config
Embeddings (batch size 32): p95 latency < 320ms per batch
Throughput goal: baseline hosted fleet to sustain 20k QPS for light payloads with autoscaling triggers
rollout_plan: Cut a release branch after feature freeze and run full acceptance harness
Deploy to staging with synthetic traffic profiles that mirror top 5 customer apps
Canary stage 1: 1% traffic for 24 hours with strict telemetry gates (latency, error-rate, cost)
Canary stage 2: 10% for 48 hours; run e2e QA on top customer scenarios
Gradual expansion: 25% for 72 hours, then full rollout if all gates pass
Fallback activation test: simulate primary model failure to verify transparent reroute to variant
Final cutover checklist signoff by PM, Eng oncall, Security, and DevEx
launch_checklist: PRs merged: API spec, runtime change, console UI, SDKs
Acceptance harness green on release branch for 3 consecutive runs
Load test: soak at 2x expected peak for 4 hours with <0.5% errors
Telemetry dashboards published and shared with oncall rotation
Runbook published: rollback steps, mitigation playbook, communication templates
Legal/compliance signoff for initial customer cohort
Customer README and migration guide published in Drive: https://drive.google.com/hosted-endpoint-launch/README
Marketing launch assets prepared (soft-launch for pilot customers)
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Model quality regressions observed after kernel changes. Mitigation: lock model variant for canary and run eval set pre/post kernel selection
Risk: Telemetry ingestion delay masks issues. Mitigation: deploy short-path metrics pipeline for canary slices with 10s granularity
Risk: Regional capacity exhaustion. Mitigation: pre-warm burst pools and enable graded fallbacks to lower-cost quantized variants
open_questions: Do we require deterministic seeding across all endpoints for reproducible e2e evals? Proposal: yes for PRD, opt-out via param
What throttling semantics do enterprise customers expect for long-lived streaming sessions? Action: capture expected profiles from 3 pilot customers
Should rerank expose per-candidate logits in addition to normalized scores? Trade-off: transparency vs payload size
